holding sharp-edged rocks with their arms
desiring to dam the salt ocean

shlokas.artha: बहु-धवल-वारि-वाहम् = filled with many white clouds · विमल-आयस-महा-असि-देह-च्छायम् = possessing the hue of a large polished steel sword · बद्ध-विहङ्गम-मालम् = decorated with rows of birds · हिम-गिरिम् = the Himālaya mountain · इव = like · मत्त-कुरर-रव-संबद्धम् = echoing with the cries of intoxicated ospreys

shlokas.artha: चारु-कल-हंस-संकुलम् = crowded with beautiful swans · स-चण्ड-संचार-सारस-आबद्ध-रवम् = filled with the loud cries of moving cranes · स-कुसुम-कण-गन्ध-वहम् = carrying the fragrance of flower pollen · समय-आगम-वारि-सङ्ग-विमल-आयामम् = appearing vast and clear due to the arrival of the monsoon rains

padaccheda.e: filled with the loud cries of moving cranes
carrying the fragrance of flower pollen
appearing vast and clear due to the arrival of the monsoon rains

shlokas.artha: सहसा = suddenly · ते = those · तरु-हरिणाः = monkeys · गिरि-सुभराः = carrying the weight of mountains · लवण-सलिल-बन्ध-आरम्भे = at the commencement of damming the salt ocean · तीर-गिरिम् = the coastal mountain · आरूढाः = ascended · राम-आगम-रुद्ध-स-भय-रिपु-संचारम् = where the movement of the terrified enemy had been blocked by Rāma’s arrival

padaccheda.e: at the commencement of damming the salt ocean
where the movement of the terrified enemy had been blocked by Rāma’s arrival

padaccheda.e: with their stable bases, peaks and slopes

fragrant with the scent of crushed kakkola and cloves

shlokas.artha: लोलम् = restless · कूल-अभिगमे = near the shore · खे = in the sky · तुङ्ग-अमल-निबद्ध-पुरु-परिणाहम् = assuming a vast, lofty and pure expanse · सुर-गङ्गा-भरण-सहम् = capable of holding the celestial Gaṅgā · गिरि-बन्ध-वरेण = by the excellent dam of mountains · लवण-सलिलम् = the salt water · रुद्धम् = was confined

padaccheda.e: beautiful with its clusters of excellent mountains entwined with rows of trees

shlokas.artha: लङ्का-आलय-तुमल-आरव-सुभर-गभीर-उरु-कुञ्ज-कन्दर-विवरम् = whose deep and large caves and mountain-groves were filled with the tumultuous sounds from the city of Laṅkā · वीणा-रव-रस-सङ्गम-सुर-गण-संकुल-महा-तमाल-च्छायम् = whose dark tamāla shade was crowded with celestial beings enjoying the melodies of the lute

padaccheda.e: whose deep and large caves and mountain-groves were filled with the tumultuous sounds from the city of Laṅkā
whose dark tamāla shade was crowded with celestial beings enjoying the melodies of the lute

shlokas.artha: स-रस-बहु-पल्लव-आविल-केसर-हिन्ताल-बद्ध-बहल-च्छायम् = which offered dense shade from bakula and hintāla trees thick with fresh leaves · ऐरावण-मद-परिमल-गन्धवह-आबद्ध-दन्ति-संरम्भ-रसम् = where the elephants’ excitement was stirred by breezes carrying the scent of Airāvaṇa's ichor

padaccheda.e: which offered dense shade from bakula and hintāla trees thick with fresh leaves
where the elephants’ excitement was stirred by breezes carrying the scent of Airāvaṇa's ichor

padaccheda.e: which had clusters of tender, attractive, swaying leaves growing in the shade of tall trees
and pomegranate groves with swaying blossoms resembling forest fires, terrifying to the deer

padaccheda.e: which echoed with the sweet chirping of birds

padaccheda.e: which had peaks of clear large gems
and large slopes reddish-yellow with vermilion marks
where the desire for nocturnal roaming was checked by the fear of encounters between brave lions and elephants

padaccheda.e: which had fearsome caves with large serpents
resounded with the loud and terrible cries of numerous birds
crowded with elephants, boars, lions, excellent cattle, and deer amidst its large sāla trees

padaccheda.e: which appeared playful with moving sprouts
whose ground was yellowish with the pollen of beautiful earth-lotuses
which possessed bakula flowers as arrows

padaccheda.e: with its peaks of pure gems and gold

padaccheda.e: possessed excellent trees bowing under the weight of fruits
adorned with attractive flower-wreaths growing nearby
Its deep caves were filled with abundant water originating from moonstones

padaccheda.e: its body crowded with elephants seeking water, with beautiful white caves flowing with liquid gold
whose trembling emerald rays, like the luster of fresh sprouts, were licked by herds of ruru deer

padaccheda.e: and the collision of high clouds making fearsome noises
which, by its connection with rows of white clouds, assumed the graceful appearance of the Himālaya mountains

padaccheda.e: delighted by the construction of the bridge over the salt sea
whose physical exhaustion was alleviated by the abundance of fruits from trees
which acted as a barrier to the gates of Laṅkā

shlokas.artha: गुरु-पणव-वेणु-गुञ्जा-भेरी-पेलु-उरु-झल्लरी-भीम-रवम् = with the terrifying sound of large drums, flutes, kettledrums, and large cymbals · ढक्का-घण्टा-तुमुलम् = tumultuous with drums and bells · सन्नद्धम् = prepared · पर-बलम् = the enemy's army · रण-आयास-सहम् = capable of enduring the fatigue of war

padaccheda.e: its stout bodies concealed in clean iron mail

padaccheda.e: equipped with swords, javelins, spears, great axes, arrows, and heavy clubs
adorned with the sentiment of heroism
with the earth shaking from the heavy movement of their horses and elephants

shlokas.artha: जल-तीर-तुङ्ग-तरु-वर-कन्दर-गिरि-भित्ति-कुञ्ज-विवर-आवासम् = residing in excellent tall trees by the water, in caves, on mountain walls, and in bower-crevices · भीमम् = formidable · तरु-हरिण-बलम् = the monkey army · सु-समिद्ध-हिमारि-किरण-माला-लोलम् = restless like the rays of the blazing sun

padaccheda.e: residing in excellent tall trees by the water, in caves, on mountain walls, and in bower-crevices
restless like the rays of the blazing sun

shlokas.artha: जल-भर-गुरु-सलिल-वाह-गण-सम-च्छायम् = which possessed the dark hue of clouds heavy with water · रावण-बलम् = the army of Rāvaṇa · अवगन्तुम् = to observe · अट्ट-तरु-मञ्च-मन्दिर-तोरण-माला-सभासु = upon watchtowers, trees, platforms, palaces, arched gateways, and assembly halls · समारूढम् = climbed

padaccheda.e: which possessed the dark hue of clouds heavy with water
upon watchtowers, trees, platforms, palaces, arched gateways, and assembly halls

padaccheda.e: having the enemy's strength revealed by spies
with a magically created head of Rāma
